assertions.subject: Patent Foramen Ovale
assertions.quote: The thrombus could travel from the left atrium into the systemic circulation, where it can, unfortunately, be delivered to the brain, causing a thromboembolic cerebrovascular accident (CVA).

assertions.subject: Patent Foramen Ovale
assertions.quote: A patent foramen ovale connects the right and left atria and is usually found as an incidental finding on an echocardiogram or after a cryptogenic stroke.

assertions.subject: Pulmonary Embolism
assertions.predicate: deep venous thrombosis (DVT) of the lower extremity
assertions.quote: The most worrisome complication of pulmonary circulation dysfunction is a pulmonary embolism, which usually arises as a deep venous thrombosis (DVT) of the lower extremity.

assertions.subject: Deep Venous Thrombosis (DVT)
assertions.quote: Rarely do DVTs occur without satisfying at least one of the three components of Virchow’s triad: hypercoagulability, endothelial damage, and venous stasis.
